sharedPrerequisites: Use the exact independently verified candidate/formal bundle and preserve the existing data/draft baseline before replacement.
Root controls the only formal application. Use a newly owned temporary repository and unique target paths; no user repository mutations. Keep current Agent/account/model/reasoning/permissions.

worktree.assertion: Inspect an ordinary local owned repository. Record HEAD, source Git index hash and tracked dirty/untracked/ignored canaries before use; no project scripts, hooks or dependencies run.

Create a new branch worktree at the explicitly selected commit into a new child directory. Require ready receipt plus actual linked-worktree Git identity/branch/HEAD and committed content; dirty/untracked/ignored source bytes and source index remain unchanged. Directory existence alone is insufficient.

Exercise one unused existing local branch and one pre-existing linked tree adoption. Their exact common repository/path/branch identity must match; adopted location is marked existing, never promoted to created ownership.

Creating or adopting alone leaves the unsent draft cwd unchanged. Only Use after fresh verification applies the location to the currently owned new draft; original draft contents and historical conversation cwd remain, and no prompt is sent.

Choose an existing target or in-use branch once. Rejection must preserve both source and target. For a saved location, the explicit two-step From list removal changes metadata only: files, branch and conversations remain.

After normal close/reopen, saved locations require recheck before use. Original drafts remain. If a genuine unknown result occurs, retain its path, display uncertainty and allow only explicit review/recheck; do not retry creation or delete material to manufacture a pass.

If a real current creation is observably in flight, cancellation is only a request and exit must stay blocked until its actual outcome. If it completes too quickly, record cancellation/active-exit as not exercised; do not call ready completion a successful cancel or terminate processes to fabricate the state.

asyncStop.assertion: First retain actual AIR v1 asyncTasks advertisement from this connection and actual spawned notification with session/task/tool ownership. Without both, the stop control must not be offered and installed task stopping remains unexercised; never infer a task ID from command/PID/history.

For a bounded owned task explicitly reported stoppable, click Stop task once. Preserve exact connection/session/task ID and official request/reply. Accepted means only request accepted; UI must wait for an official task result. No OS kill or second connection substitute.

Record the subsequent official task event and any bounded owned marker timeline separately. stopped may establish the reported task terminal, not that every subprocess ended; completed means natural/actual completion and must not be relabeled stopped.

Task stop does not synthesize a reply/tool terminal, cancel the reply, or consume/pause unrelated queued drafts. Existing reply-stop queue behavior stays distinct. Compare pre/post unsent groups and original tool/reply events.

Repeated clicks while requested/accepted/unknown remain guarded. Changing conversation or viewing history cannot reuse old live ownership. If rejection/timeout/disconnection actually occurs, retain unknown/rejected state and configuration/exit protection; do not provoke loss or claim those error paths were native-tested when they were not.
